description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 2).  The residue of #1587 (s484a),
in the same family as #1642.

#1587 made `eval 'package X { … }'` work by handing the Package statement back
into ONE region segment and letting `_lower_block`'s `if ($blk)` arm run.  Its
gate in `Pl::Parser2` is:

    if ($self->_eval_safe_leading_stmts(\@lead)
        && (!$erased || _eval_literal_only_stmts(\@trail))) { ...collapse... }

`$erased` is true only for the FLATTENED bare-block spelling.  The TRAILING
whitelist is correctly gated on it -- the comment says so: "a TOP-LEVEL block
form (nothing erased) may be followed by anything" -- but the LEADING one is
NOT, and by the same argument it should be: when nothing is erased, the
leading statements are at the eval's own top level and the region they are
swept into is `pkg => $root_pkg`, i.e. exactly the package they already ran in.
The whitelist exists to make `*package*` = X unobservable (#240's
silent-wrong); with the block form there is no X binding around them.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl) -- both refuse today, and the only leading
statement is an assignment to a QUALIFIED global:

    $main::result = "";
    eval q{
        $main::result .= "a(".__PACKAGE__.")";
        package Foo { $main::result .= "b(".__PACKAGE__.")"; }
        $main::result .= "e(".__PACKAGE__.")";
    };
    print "err=[$@] result=[$main::result]\n";

    perl:  err=[] result=[a(main)b(Foo)e(main)]
    PCL :  err=[PCL: unsupported in string eval: multiple package sections
                at (eval 2) line 1.]  result=[]

WHAT IT COSTS: t/comp/package_block.t DIFF 0/7 -- all 7 rows fail, no
shortfall.  The leading-whitelist fix alone reaches rows 2 and 3 (row 3 is the
probe above with an empty block; row 2 is `package Foo 11 { ; }` +
`package Bar 22 { … }`, which is TWO blockforms and stays refused).  The other
five need more: row 1 NESTED blockforms (`package Foo { package Bar::Baz { … } }`
-- five segments, two blockforms, the #1642 boundary), row 4 the `Missing right
curly` syntax error (NS:Error compatibility for invalid Perl input), row 5
`__LINE__` inside an eval'd block form, rows 6-7 `goto LABEL` INTO and OUT OF a
package block plus its `Use of "goto" ...` warning text (NS:Warnings-gated
diagnostics are absent).  So the honest sizing is 2 of 7 for the cheap fix.

MANDATORY BAR (a refusal stops firing): the gate-SET scan over BOTH
populations (`tools/gate-set-scan.pl`, compared against a base worktree),
plus corpus-diff and the sweep's TOTAL/LOST -- the s372 rule.  And PROBE THE
BREAKING CASE: a leading statement that reads an UNQUALIFIED global or calls a
bareword is the #240 shape the whitelist was written for; with `$erased`
false it should still be safe, and that claim is what the probe must
establish, not assume.
subject: The eval BLOCK-form `package` collapse still gates its LEADING statements on the flattened-shape whitelist, so `eval 'STMT; package Foo { … } STMT'` refuses although nothing is erased -- t/comp/package_block.t's 7 rows (#1587/#1642 residue)
